content.transcript:
Receptionist: City TV, how can I help you? 
Student: Hello, I'm calling about the Work Experience Opportunity, WEO 5, that I saw advertised. 
Receptionist: Yes, of course. We have several vacancies for students interested in media. Are you in your last year at school? 
Student: Yes, I am. The notice mentioned an excellent salary for a permanent position. Does the work experience offer payment? 
Receptionist: The work experience itself is unpaid, but it's a great way to see if you enjoy working in news, theatre, or music production. Many of our work experience students go on to get permanent positions with us. 
Student: That sounds interesting. What should I do next? 
Receptionist: You'll need to send us your CV and a cover letter explaining why you're interested in this opportunity. You can find the email address on our website.

content.transcript: Presenter: Listen to the four interviews and match the statements. Reporter: Mrs Ibrahim, do you think your job is worthwhile? Mrs Ibrahim: Of course being a teacher is a worthwhile job. I share what I know with my students. Every day they learn a little more from me. And I help to prepare them for life after school. So my job is definitely worthwhile. I help to build the future of the country. Reporter: Mary, is your job worthwhile? Mary: Of course it's a worthwhile job. We save lives. We also save people's houses and their places of work. We often have to go to a factory to put out a fire. Factories are dangerous places. But the most important part of my work is teaching people about fire prevention, about how to make sure fires don't start. Reporter: Mr Habib, do you do a worthwhile job? Mr Habib: I enjoy being a businessman. And I think it's a valuable job. People think we just make money for ourselves, but that's not true. We business people also make a lot of money for the country. We create the money to pay for nurses and teachers and firefighters. And we create jobs for other people. Reporter: And finally, Miss Ahmed, I'm sure your job is worthwhile. Miss Ahmed: Well, I'm a hospital nurse. And people don't seem to think this is a very worthwhile job. We work very long hours and they don't pay us much. But I enjoy my work. I take care of people who are ill and help them get better. I most enjoy looking after children. It makes me very happy to see a sick child get well. Yes, I do think my job is worthwhile.

content.passage:
Patrick's ambition after leaving school is to become a doctor. However, he is not very good at Chemistry or Biology. His best subject is Mathematics. For the last year he has been going to evening classes in first-aid. He is adventurous and when he can, he goes underwater swimming.

Diana is very efficient and likes organizing things. Since the beginning of the year she has been planning all the class trips and outings. She writes all the letters and notices on her computer. Her best subject is English, but she enjoys Mathematics more. At the weekend she goes sailing and she is the secretary of the local sailing club. She would like to go into Government Administration.

Andrew is not very good at any subjects at school although he will probably pass his final examinations. He has a driving licence and every weekend he drives out into the country and then walks for hours. He is very interested in nature and has been reading about trees, plants and flowers for almost two years. He would like to work in the country. He is very hard-working and gets on well with people.

Justin has two very different hobbies: driving his father's new car in the country, and cooking. He spends most Saturdays driving along muddy roads. On Sundays he cooks all the meals for the whole family. He has been doing this since he was 12. His best subjects are Mathematics and Sport. Both his parents are teachers, but he would like to go into business.

Clare has been collecting folk-music CDs for three years. She now has 150. She has lots of friends and she likes playing her music to them. One day she would like to sing or play on television. At school her best subjects are History and Music. She has a good speaking voice and often acts in the plays put on by the school drama group.

Fareeda is a very helpful young woman and is very good at helping others in her class. She has been driving for six months and at the weekend she takes her disabled young sister in her parents' car. At school she is excellent at History, but she does not want to go to college. She wants to help other people in some way, perhaps as social worker.

activities.title: Grammar Rules Check
activities.instruction: Reading time! 📖 Read carefully and the statements about the Present Perfect tenses from Pupil's Book page 20. Decide if they are true or false.

statements.statement: The Present Perfect Continuous emphasizes how long an action has been going on.
statements.explanation: Correct. The continuous form focuses on the duration of the action.

statements.statement: The Present Perfect Simple is used for actions that have been happening very recently.
statements.explanation: Incorrect. The continuous tense usually refers to recent actions. The simple tense can refer to actions from a long time ago.

statements.statement: Verbs like 'know', 'believe', and 'need' are commonly used in the continuous tense.
statements.explanation: Incorrect. These are stative verbs and are not usually used with the continuous tense.

statements.statement: We use the Present Perfect Continuous to talk about the present effects of a recent, continuous action.
statements.explanation: Correct. For example: 'It has been raining, so the ground is wet.'

statements.statement: After 'would like' or 'would prefer', you must use the -ing form of the verb.
statements.explanation: Incorrect. After 'would like/love/prefer/hate', you must use the 'to + infinitive' form.

content.transcript:
Speaker 1: Would you like to work abroad? Would you like to help people in poorer countries? The World Aid Organization is looking for young people to help in the following areas. Education: we need young men and women to help with teaching reading and writing to children at Primary Schools. Health: we need young people who want to get experience of work in clinics. You must be in good health, under 20 years old and be ready to live abroad for at least 6 months. Send for an application form to P.O. Box 791.
Speaker 2: The famous Gate Restaurant is right in the centre of town. We are looking for people to train as cooks. We serve food from all over the world, so this is a wonderful opportunity for a young man who wants to start a career in the restaurant business. Come and see us for an interview. Ring 35692 and make an appointment.
Speaker 3: We know that many of you have booked your holidays at the Sunrise Travel Agency. And now we have a vacancy for a clerk. It will be your job to sell holidays and travel tickets to the public. You must be able to use a computer and speak at least one foreign language. Both men and women may apply. Write to P.O. Box 3815, giving details of yourself, and enclose a photograph. This could be the start of a very rewarding career.
Speaker 4: The Television Company is looking for a young man or woman to train as a reporter and presenter of news programmes. After training in this country, the successful applicant must be ready to work abroad in Europe or the United States for at least three months. He or she must have a good speaking voice, be interested in news and politics, and speak English fluently. Telephone 9582 for more details and an application form.
Speaker 5: Do you like working with animals? Are you interested in the environment? Are you interested in saving rare animals? There is a vacancy at the zoo for a trainee zookeeper. You must be male, healthy and ready to work hard. Write to P.O. Box 1269 for more details.
Speaker 6: We fight crime. We make sure that people drive safely. We help and protect people. We offer a long, secure and rewarding career to men and women. Who are we? The Police. Come and join us. Ring 4186 and find out more.

activities.title: Grammar: Present Perfect Tenses
activities.instruction: Complete the sentences with the correct form of the verb in brackets (present perfect simple or continuous).
activities.compensates: Provides interactive practice for the language focus (Present perfect simple and continuous) mentioned in the Teacher Guide.

content.feedback: Great effort! You've successfully completed the sentences. Keep it up! 🚀

sentences.text: I ___ (develop) a strong interest in photography over the last few years.

blanks.hint: Use the present perfect simple for a completed action with relevance to the present.

sentences.explanation: We use the present perfect simple ('have developed') to talk about something that happened at an unspecified time in the past but is relevant now.

sentences.text: Recently, I ___ (take) a course on digital editing to improve my skills.

blanks.hint: Use the present perfect continuous for a recent, ongoing activity.

sentences.explanation: We use the present perfect continuous ('have been taking') to emphasize the duration of a recent activity.

sentences.text: I ___ (always / be) a dedicated reader of your newspaper.

blanks.hint: Use the present perfect simple with 'always' for a state that continues to the present.

sentences.explanation: The present perfect simple ('have always been') is used with state verbs like 'be' to describe a state that started in the past and continues.

sentences.text: My friends and I ___ (create) a school blog for the past six months.

blanks.hint: Use the present perfect continuous to emphasize the duration of an action.

sentences.explanation: The phrase 'for the past six months' emphasizes the duration, so the present perfect continuous ('have been creating') is appropriate.

As for my hobbies, I have been an active member of the school photography club for two years.
Although I do not have formal work experience, I have written several articles for our school magazine.
I am ambitious and eager to learn from your experienced team.
